description: An introduction to force and its effects, the meaning and calculation of density, floating and sinking, pressure in solids and liquids, and the relationship between mass and weight.

mcq.questionText: A force is best described as:
mcq.explanation: A force acts on a body as a push or a pull, changing its motion or shape. Exam Tip: Force can start, stop, speed up, slow down, turn or change the shape of an object.

mcq.questionText: The SI unit of force is the:
mcq.explanation: The SI unit of force is the newton (N). Exam Tip: newton (N) = force; joule (J) = energy/work; pascal (Pa) = pressure.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is an effect of a force?

options.text: Changing the colour of a body
Changing the speed or shape of a body
Changing the taste of a body
Changing the smell of a body

mcq.explanation: A force can change a body's speed, direction or shape. Exam Tip: Effects include start/stop motion, change speed, direction and shape, not colour, taste or smell.

mcq.questionText: The density of a substance is defined as:
mcq.explanation: Density is defined as mass divided by volume. Exam Tip: density = mass / volume; option c is upside down.

mcq.questionText: The SI unit of density is:
mcq.explanation: Density = mass (kg) / volume (m3) = kg/m3. Exam Tip: use kg/m3 (or g/cm3); note the per cubic metre.

mcq.questionText: A block has a mass of 300 g and a volume of 100 cm3. Its density is:
mcq.explanation: Density = 300 / 100 = 3 g/cm3. Exam Tip: keep units consistent (g and cm3 give g/cm3); option c divides the wrong way.

mcq.questionText: An object floats in water if its density is:
mcq.explanation: An object less dense than water floats. Exam Tip: less dense than the liquid floats, more dense sinks; water = 1 g/cm3.

mcq.questionText: An object sinks in water if its density is:
mcq.explanation: An object denser than water sinks. Exam Tip: denser than water (greater than 1 g/cm3) sinks; a stone sinks while dry wood floats.
Pressure is defined as force divided by area. Exam Tip: pressure = force / area; more area spreads the force, giving less pressure.

mcq.questionText: The SI unit of pressure is the:
mcq.explanation: The SI unit of pressure is the pascal (Pa), equal to one newton per square metre. Exam Tip: 1 Pa = 1 N/m2; pascal = pressure, newton = force.

mcq.questionText: A force of 20 N acts on an area of 4 m2. The pressure produced is:
mcq.explanation: Pressure = 20 / 4 = 5 Pa. Exam Tip: divide force by area; option a multiplies instead.

mcq.questionText: A sharp knife cuts more easily than a blunt one because a sharp edge has:

options.text: A larger area, giving less pressure
A smaller area, giving greater pressure

mcq.explanation: A smaller area gives greater pressure for the same force. Exam Tip: small area = high pressure (knives, nails, pins); large area = low pressure.

mcq.questionText: Why do heavy tractors have wide tyres?

options.text: To increase the pressure on the soil
To reduce the pressure on the soil so they do not sink

mcq.explanation: Wide tyres have a large area, spreading the weight and reducing pressure. Exam Tip: large area = low pressure, which stops heavy vehicles sinking into soft ground.

mcq.questionText: The pressure in a liquid increases with:

options.text: The shape of the container only

mcq.explanation: Deeper liquid has more weight above it, so pressure increases with depth. Exam Tip: liquid pressure increases with depth and density; a dam is thicker at the bottom.

mcq.questionText: The mass of a body is 5 kg and its weight on Earth (g = 10 N/kg) is:
mcq.explanation: Weight = mass x g = 5 x 10 = 50 N. Exam Tip: weight (N) = mass (kg) x g (10 N/kg); mass is in kg while weight is a force in newtons.

fib.questionText: A push or a pull acting on a body is called a ____.
fib.explanation: A force is any push or pull that acts on a body. Exam Tip: Force changes motion or shape; its unit is the newton.

fib.questionText: The SI unit of force is the ____.
fib.explanation: Force is measured in newtons. Exam Tip: Named after Isaac Newton; symbol N.

fib.questionText: Density is calculated using the formula density = mass / ____.
fib.explanation: Density equals mass divided by volume. Exam Tip: density = mass / volume; rearranged, mass = density x volume.

fib.questionText: An object will float in a liquid if its density is ____ than that of the liquid.
fib.explanation: A body less dense than the liquid floats. Exam Tip: Less dense floats; more dense sinks.

fib.questionText: Pressure is calculated using the formula pressure = force / ____.
fib.explanation: Pressure equals force divided by area. Exam Tip: P = F/A; its unit is the pascal (N/m2).

fib.questionText: The SI unit of pressure is the ____.
fib.explanation: Pressure is measured in pascals. Exam Tip: 1 pascal = 1 newton per square metre.

fib.questionText: The density of pure water is 1 g/cm3 or ____ kg/m3.
fib.explanation: 1 g/cm3 is equal to 1000 kg/m3. Exam Tip: Water's density (1000 kg/m3) is the benchmark for floating and sinking.

fib.questionText: The pull of gravity on a body is called its ____.
fib.explanation: Weight is the pull of gravity on a body. Exam Tip: Weight = mass x g; weight is a force while mass is in kilograms.

fib.questionText: For the same force, a ____ area of contact produces a greater pressure.
fib.explanation: A smaller contact area concentrates the same force, giving greater pressure. Exam Tip: Small area = high pressure (knife edge, nail tip).

fib.questionText: Pressure in a liquid increases as the ____ increases.
fib.explanation: The deeper you go, the greater the weight of liquid above, so pressure rises. Exam Tip: Liquid pressure depends on depth and density, not container shape.

tf.questionText: A force can change the shape, speed or direction of a body.
tf.explanation: Changing shape, speed and direction are exactly the effects a force can produce. Exam Tip: These effects define what a force does.

tf.questionText: The SI unit of force is the joule.
tf.explanation: Force is measured in newtons; the joule is the unit of energy. Exam Tip: Force = newton; energy = joule. The two are often swapped.

tf.questionText: Density is mass divided by volume.
tf.explanation: Density is defined as mass divided by volume. Exam Tip: density = mass / volume.

tf.questionText: An object denser than water will float on water.
tf.explanation: A body more dense than the liquid sinks rather than floats. Exam Tip: More dense than the liquid sinks.

tf.questionText: Pressure is force divided by area.
tf.explanation: Pressure is defined as force divided by area. Exam Tip: pressure = force / area; unit pascal (N/m2).

tf.questionText: A sharp needle produces less pressure than a blunt one for the same force.
tf.explanation: A sharp point has a very small area, so it produces greater pressure, not less. Exam Tip: Sharp point = small area = high pressure.

tf.questionText: Pressure in a liquid increases with depth.
tf.explanation: The deeper the point, the greater the weight of liquid above and the higher the pressure. Exam Tip: Dams are thicker at the base because pressure is greatest at the bottom.

tf.questionText: The weight of a body is the same as its mass.
tf.explanation: Mass measures the amount of matter in kilograms, while weight is the gravitational force in newtons. Exam Tip: Mass is in kg; weight is a force in newtons (weight = mass x g).

tf.questionText: Wide tyres reduce the pressure a vehicle exerts on the ground.
tf.explanation: Wide tyres spread the weight over a larger area, lowering the pressure. Exam Tip: Large area = low pressure.

tf.questionText: The SI unit of density is kg/m3.
tf.explanation: Density in SI units is kilograms per cubic metre. Exam Tip: kg/m3 (SI) or g/cm3; 1 g/cm3 = 1000 kg/m3.

summary.correctAnswer: A push or a pull that acts on a body and can change its motion or shape.
summary.explanation: A force can start, stop, speed up, slow down, turn or deform an object. Exam Tip: List the effects of a force clearly in exams.

summary.correctAnswer: The SI unit of force, symbol N, named after Isaac Newton.
summary.explanation: One newton is the force needed to accelerate 1 kg at 1 m/s2. Exam Tip: newton = force; do not confuse with joule (energy) or pascal (pressure).

summary.correctAnswer: A force can start or stop motion, change speed or direction, and change the shape of a body.
summary.explanation: These are the standard effects of a force and do not include colour, taste or smell. Exam Tip: Remember start/stop, change speed/direction, change shape.

summary.correctAnswer: Density is the mass of a substance divided by its volume.
summary.explanation: It tells how much matter is packed into a given space. Exam Tip: Rearranged, mass = density x volume and volume = mass / density.

summary.correctAnswer: The SI unit of density, kilograms per cubic metre.
summary.explanation: Density can also be given in g/cm3, where 1 g/cm3 = 1000 kg/m3. Exam Tip: Keep mass and volume units consistent when calculating.

summary.correctAnswer: An object floats if it is less dense than the liquid and sinks if it is more dense than the liquid.
summary.explanation: Water has a density of 1 g/cm3 (1000 kg/m3), the benchmark for comparison. Exam Tip: Compare the object's density with the liquid's density.

summary.correctAnswer: Pressure is the force acting per unit area.
summary.explanation: For the same force, a smaller area gives greater pressure. Exam Tip: P = F/A; spreading the force over more area lowers pressure.

summary.correctAnswer: The SI unit of pressure, equal to one newton per square metre (N/m2).
summary.explanation: 1 Pa = 1 N/m2. Exam Tip: pascal = pressure; do not confuse it with the newton.

summary.correctAnswer: Weight is the pull of gravity on a body, equal to mass multiplied by gravitational field strength g.
summary.explanation: On Earth g is about 10 N/kg, so a 5 kg body weighs about 50 N. Exam Tip: Weight is a force in newtons; mass is in kilograms.

summary.correctAnswer: Pressure in a liquid increases with depth and with the density of the liquid.
summary.explanation: Deeper points carry more weight of liquid above them, so pressure is greatest at the bottom. Exam Tip: A dam is built thicker at its base for this reason.

hoq.questionText: A rectangular metal block has a mass of 240 g and measures 4 cm x 3 cm x 2 cm. Calculate its density and state whether it floats or sinks in water (water = 1 g/cm3).
hoq.explanation: Volume = 4 x 3 x 2 = 24 cm3, so density = 240 / 24 = 10 g/cm3. Being denser than water, the block sinks. Exam Tip: Find the volume first, then divide mass by volume, then compare with water.

hoq.questionText: A brick of weight 40 N rests on its largest face (contact area 0.02 m2) and then on its smallest face (contact area 0.005 m2). Compare the pressure in the two positions.

options.text: Largest face: 2000 Pa; smallest face: 8000 Pa - pressure is greater on the smaller face
Largest face: 8000 Pa; smallest face: 2000 Pa
Largest face: 2000 Pa; smallest face: 2000 Pa

hoq.explanation: On the largest face, pressure = 40 / 0.02 = 2000 Pa; on the smallest face, pressure = 40 / 0.005 = 8000 Pa, so the smaller area gives greater pressure. Exam Tip: The same weight on a smaller area gives greater pressure (P = F/A).

hoq.questionText: Oil has density 0.8 g/cm3 and water 1.0 g/cm3. A cork (0.24 g/cm3) and a metal nut (8 g/cm3) are dropped into a glass containing both liquids. Predict the arrangement from top to bottom.

options.text: Cork floats on top, oil layer, then water, metal nut at the bottom
Metal nut on top, water, oil, cork at the bottom

hoq.explanation: Ordering the densities gives cork 0.24 < oil 0.8 < water 1.0 < metal 8, so the least dense floats highest and the most dense sinks lowest. Exam Tip: Arrange by density - least dense on top, most dense at the bottom.
